issues.problem: Facts described only as 'e.g. about hiring or growth metrics' rather than a concrete message text, leaving the compiler to invent content without a fixed anchor.
issues.repair: Specify a concrete message_text for message_freeman (any off-topic content) so the negative is fully deterministic before compilation.

rationale: The route WORKSPACE→WORKSPACE_MEMBERSHIP→USER→MESSAGE correctly reflects the prompt's 'member named Morgan who personally posted about X' (membership plus authorship, not mere channel co-presence). The underspecified mode is justified: two distinct, equally valid Morgan+message combinations exist in two different workspaces (Test Workspace/Morgan Stanley and the newly added Nimbus Robotics/Morgan Reyes), and the user gives no disambiguating detail, so resolution requires an arbitrary/unauthorized choice — matching the underspecified definition. Negatives are well-targeted and non-trivial: Morgan Freeman (right name, wrong/no topic message) and Devon Park (right topic and workspace, wrong name) each isolate exactly one leg of the required conjunction, and Łukasz Kowalski gives a same-workspace/different-topic distractor. The new workspace_beta addition is a legitimate planned addition (not yet in seed) rather than a defect, consistent with allowed design-stage additions. Access plan (users.list/users.info + search.messages per workspace) uses only supported, documented operations, and the answer_attributes (teams.team_name/team_id) are real, non-derived columns. No banned attributes (timestamps, reactions, etc.) are requested, and the task is a plain read/identify obligation matching the prompt's actual ask. The only shortcoming is the vaguely specified content for the off-topic negative message, a minor quality nit rather than a validity defect.
